title: Dissolving & Mixing
strapline: Stir sugar into warm water, watch it vanish, and find out what dissolves and what doesn't.
intent: Children investigate change — some things dissolve and disappear, others don't, some can't come back.
Children predict, test and sort materials by what happens when they meet water.
Children observe closely and describe what they see, using real scientific words.
Children explore variables — warm water versus cold, more stirring, more powder.
Children ask genuine questions and expect to find out by trying.
implementation: Offer clear jars, warm and cold water, spoons, and a tray of things to test — sugar, salt, sand, flour, rice, oil.
Ask children to predict before each one: 'do you think this will disappear or stay?'
Let them stir, watch closely and sort the materials into 'dissolves' and 'doesn't'.
Introduce a variable honestly — 'does it dissolve faster in warm or cold water?' — and test it.
Model the vocabulary — dissolve, disappear, mixture, stir, faster, cloudy, clear.
Talk about which changes can be undone and which can't, linking to cooking and everyday life.
Follow the children's own 'what if we tried...' ideas and let the investigation grow.
key_questions: Do you think this one will disappear or stay?
What happened when you stirred it in?
Which ones dissolved and which stayed the same?
Does it dissolve faster in the warm water or the cold?
What shall we try next — what do you want to find out?

impact.text: Children investigate change, discovering what dissolves, what doesn't, and what can't come back.
Children predict, test and sort materials by what happens in water.
Children observe closely and describe what they see with real scientific words.
Children explore variables — warm versus cold, more stirring — and compare results.
Children ask real questions and follow their own 'what if' ideas.
Children pour, stir and handle the equipment with growing control.

enhancements: Clear jars, warm and cold water and stirring spoons.
A tray of materials to test — sugar, salt, sand, flour, rice, oil.
A prediction chart to mark guesses before testing.
Pipettes, funnels and jugs for careful pouring.
Magnifiers for watching the change up close.
A recording sheet with pictures to note what happened.

playing_exploring: Children explore what water does to all sorts of materials.
They test their own 'what if we mixed this?' ideas freely.
active_learning: Children stir and watch patiently to see the change through.
They repeat tests to be sure of the result.
creating_thinking: Children predict what will happen and check against what they see.
They change one thing — warmth, stirring — and reason about why the result changed.
